subject: Sustained tokens/sec commitment & hot-pool ops playbook — renewal negotiation
messages:
From: Daniel Park <daniel.park@clearwave.ai>
To: Kimberly Park <kimberly_park@redwood.ai>
Cc: ClearWave Cloud SE <se@clearwave.ai>, procurement@clearwave.ai
Date: Wed, 02 Dec 2026 09:12:00 -0800
Subject: Renewal: committed pool sizing + throughput guardrails

Hi Kimberly —

Thanks again for the renewal packet. A few follow-ups from our infra/ops team: as we scale new features in H2 next year we need a more explicit sustained tokens/sec commitment for the reserved pool and a short playbook for how Redwood will handle short-duration bursts and graceful degradations.

Specifically:
- We plan to increase inference concurrency across users (multi-tenant workload) starting Feb; want a sustained tokens/sec commitment tied to our reserved pool.
- We expect short 30–60s bursts during batch runs; need a plan for bursts without cascading errors.
- Our procurement team also requested sample monitoring outputs and how SLO violations will be measured and credited.

Can you draft an addendum that includes an ops playbook (pre-warm strategy, KV cache priming, fallbacks) and a concrete tokens/sec guarantee for the reserved pool?

Thanks,
Daniel
Daniel Park
Head of Platform Operations — ClearWave


From: Kimberly Park <kimberly_park@redwood.ai>
To: Daniel Park <daniel.park@clearwave.ai>
Cc: Marcus Lin <marcus_lin@redwood.ai>, Monica Patel <monica_patel@redwood.ai>
Date: Wed, 02 Dec 2026 11:08:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Renewal: committed pool sizing + throughput guardrails

Daniel —

Appreciate the detail. I spoke with our capacity and SRE leads this morning and sketched a proposal. High level summary:

1) Commitment: Reserved pool will be sized to cover a sustained 600k tokens/sec for steady-state production traffic, with a burst tier up to 1.0M tokens/sec for 45s (subject to burst credits). We map the pool to an explicit GPU count (48x V100-equivalent reserved GPUs) for contract clarity.

2) Measurement & SLO: Redwood measures sustained throughput at the pool gate (edge + routing layer). SLO is defined as 99.5% of 1-minute windows in the billed month meeting >= 95% of committed sustained tokens/sec (600k). Missed SLOs trigger a service credit equal to 2% of monthly reserved fees per missed SLO event, up to a 20% cap.

3) Burst handling & fallbacks: For bursts beyond the 45s / 1.0M tokens/sec allowance we will: (a) automatically route overflow to a dedicated burst buffer pool (best-effort) and (b) serve degraded but correct responses using a compatible quantized model variant if necessary. We will notify ClearWave via webhooks when the fallback is in effect.

4) Ops playbook (short): pre-warm KV cache for top-10 prefixes, schedule rolling cache-pop jobs during low-traffic windows, and provide a 2-hour pre-warm SLA before major product launches. Maintenance windows will be agreed monthly.

I attached a draft addendum and a sample workbook with expected token burn by route. Can you confirm the ClearWave side of the ramp (dates + targeted peak QPS) so we can finalize GPU mapping and pricing?

Best,
Kimberly
Kimberly Park
Account Executive — Redwood Inference
From: Marcus Lin <marcus_lin@redwood.ai>
To: Daniel Park <daniel.park@clearwave.ai>, Kimberly Park <kimberly_park@redwood.ai>
Cc: Monica Patel <monica_patel@redwood.ai>
Date: Thu, 03 Dec 2026 10:25:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Renewal: committed pool sizing + throughput guardrails

Daniel —

Quick technical notes from capacity:
- 48 reserved GPUs (our equivalent configuration) maps to the 600k sustained tokens/sec target assuming mixed prompt lengths with a median response size of ~128 tokens. If your median grows to 256 tokens we will need to scale the pool or adjust the committed tokens/sec.
- Burst credits: we model bursts as 45s windows and apply a rolling burst budget; sustained back-to-back bursts will be throttled per the fallback.
- SLO measurement: we compute tokens/sec at the pool egress aggregated every 15s and evaluate the 1-minute windows for the SLO. Raw logs and 15s rollups will be shared to your SE bucket.

Action items for engineering: please share any scheduled release dates (show of hands: Feb 10 launch?) so we can align the pre-warm job.

Marcus
Marcus Lin
Head of Capacity — Redwood Inference

From: Daniel Park <daniel.park@clearwave.ai>
To: Kimberly Park <kimberly_park@redwood.ai>, Marcus Lin <marcus_lin@redwood.ai>
Cc: procurement@clearwave.ai
Date: Fri, 04 Dec 2026 08:40:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Renewal: committed pool sizing + throughput guardrails

Thanks Marcus — that mapping makes sense. A few clarifications from procurement/ops:
- Procurement wants the credit ladder written into the addendum with exact thresholds and an example calculation.
- Ops wants the webhook payload schema and an SLA for notification timing (we requested 2 minutes for critical fallback events).
- We will confirm launch dates today (tentative Feb 11 internal pilot, Feb 24 public).

On credits: we'd prefer a 5% monthly credit for a single SLO miss given the risk profile; if Redwood can provide more comprehensive monitoring exports and an independently verifiable measurement point (we suggested a daily token counter file), procurement is willing to consider 2% as proposed.

Daniel

From: Kimberly Park <kimberly_park@redwood.ai>
To: Daniel Park <daniel.park@clearwave.ai>, Marcus Lin <marcus_lin@redwood.ai>, Monica Patel <monica_patel@redwood.ai>, Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>
Date: Tue, 08 Dec 2026 16:45:00 -0800
Subject: Final: draft addendum and ops playbook (for legal/procurement review)

Daniel —

Attached is an updated addendum (sustained-throughput-addendum v2) and an operations playbook that addresses the procurement & ops asks:
- Credit ladder: 1 missed SLO in a month = 3% credit; 2–3 misses = 6% credit; >3 misses = 12% credit (cap 20%). Example calculations included.
- Measurement exports: 15s rollup CSVs + daily aggregate token counter file will be exported to the ClearWave SE bucket. We also include a verification snippet mapping your sample client logs to our measurement (see attached usage_sample_logs_202611.csv).
- Webhooks: we will send a critical-fallback webhook within 90s of the event; non-critical notifications within 15 minutes. Payload schema is in the addendum.
- Ramp schedule: we will add 12 GPUs on Jan 10, 2027 and a further 12 GPUs on Feb 1, 2027 to reach the 48-GPU baseline. Reserved billing will reflect the ramp (pro rata) until full reservation date.

Next steps: if procurement confirms the credit ladder and legal signs off on the measurement/export language, I will hand the addendum to Legal for final review and get a DocuSign ready. If you want a joint ops runbook review session, Marcus, Monica and I can host a 45-minute call next week.

Thanks — attaching the addendum draft and workbook now.

Best,
Kimberly Park
Account Executive — Redwood Inference

Attachments: sustained_throughput_addendum_draft.docx (draft addendum), clearwave_capacity_workbook.xlsx (capacity and cost workbook), usage_sample_logs_202611.csv (sample measurement mapping)
